Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects how she sees objects at different distances. She sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child had fluid buildup in her ears a couple of times. It affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up‚ but we monitor her ears regularly now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: None reported respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child experiences cardiovascular issues, specifically a higher risk of heart-related conditions like holes in the heart chambers and structural changes requiring monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of children with KBG syndrome experience heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves and holes in the heart chambers, which necessitate follow-up and potential medical intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child faces challenges with digestion and feeding, experiencing difficulty swallowing and sensitivity to certain food textures and tastes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly struggle with feeding difficulties, and some develop sensitivities to specific foods that trigger digestive discomfort. Research suggests that dietary restrictions and avoiding certain foods may provide temporary relief, but a comprehensive understanding of what triggers reactions is crucial.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our child exhibits neurological characteristics such as brain anomalies and susceptibility to seizures, indicating a heightened risk of neurological complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Studies show that approximately 15% of children with KBG syndrome exhibit neurological features, including brain anomalies and susceptibility to seizures. Management strategies should focus on reducing seizure frequency and intensity while ensuring adequate neurological function.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Our child suffers from recurrent otitis media and glue ear, leading to hearing difficulties and frequent visits to ENT specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media and glue ear are relatively common in children with KBG syndrome, affecting their ability to hear clearly and potentially delaying the acquisition of key developmental milestones.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: Our child requires regular ophthalmological checks due to vision issues such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), which impact her ability to perform everyday tasks without corrective lenses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems are quite prevalent among children with KBG syndrome, including conditions such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness, which can hinder normal daily activities and limit opportunities for outdoor play and academic pursuits.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our child faces unique dental challenges, including a higher incidence of tooth fractures and sensitivity to certain foods, highlighting the importance of thorough dental hygiene practices and sensitivity towards specific food textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are widespread among children with KBG syndrome, with a notable increase in the likelihood of developing weak enamel and sensitivity to certain foods, emphasizing the necessity of vigilant dental care routines.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: Our child shows delays in various developmental areas, particularly concerning fine motor skills and coordination, impacting her ability to participate in classroom activities and engage with peers on a similar level.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome frequently encounter challenges in areas such as fine motor development, coordination, and cognitive abilities, contributing to delays in key developmental milestones and the need for additional educational support and accommodations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Our child displays behavioral differences, including autism spectrum traits and neurodevelopmental disorders, which influence her interactions with others and her approach to routine and novel situations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural and developmental differences are common among children with KBG syndrome, characterized by autism spectrum traits, learning disabilities, and varying degrees of cognitive impairment, underscoring the importance of tailored interventions and therapeutic approaches.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our child presents with skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), which contribute to her unique anatomical features and impact her ability to perform certain tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies are relatively common among children with KBG syndrome, increasing the likelihood of conditions such as shortened fingers, irregular bone structures, and susceptibility to injuries sustained during play or accidents, reinforcing the significance of targeted orthodontic and injury prevention measures.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5.
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
d) Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
e) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
f) Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).

This completes the clinical report following the specified 13-category schema.

b) Recommendations for Screening and Treatments:
- Regular dental check-ups are crucial for maintaining good oral hygiene and preventing infections like periodontal disease. Regular dental cleanings and fluoride treatments can help prevent cavities and gum disease.

b) Recommendations for Screening and Treatments:

b) Recommendations for Screening and Treatments:

- Regular audiologic evaluations and consideration of myringotomy tubes (grommets) for selected children with recurrent otitis media are advisable.

- Regular ophthalmic examinations are essential, particularly for detecting and treating glaucoma and refractive errors.

- Regular dermatological checks are advised, especially for managing skin infections and folliculitis.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: N/A.

These can lead to symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and persistent cough, particularly during physical activity. A recent study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome had a valvular anomaly requiring observation and treatment. Regular follow-up echocardiograms and EKGs are recommended to monitor for potential complications.
How this affects the patient: N/A.
How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly exhibit feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. These can result from various factors, including weak jaw musculature, tongue-tie, and neurological involvement. Management strategies include dietary modifications, therapeutic feeding tubes, and speech therapy.
How this affects the patient: N/A.
How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. Autoimmune disorders such as Type 1 diabetes, thyroid disease, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis have been reported in some affected individuals. Vaccinations should be administered according to standard protocols, but immunocomplex-dependent reactions can occur. Regular monitoring and consideration of prophylactic vaccinations are advised.
How this affects the patient: N/A.
How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: Occasionally, children with KBG syndrome display episodes of synkinesis, where voluntary movements are accompanied by involuntary ones. Synkinesis can manifest as twitching or spasms in response to normal movement. Additionally, there is a higher incidence of seizures compared to the general population. Neurological evaluations, including brain imaging and electromyography, might provide additional insights into neurological function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient: An ear infection called otitis media is quite common in children with KBG syndrome, potentially leading to temporary hearing loss or conductive hearing issues. Regular audiometric screenings and timely antibiotic treatments are crucial for preventing prolonged hearing impairments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient: Vision-related issues such as astigmatism and shortsightedness (myopia) are relatively frequent among children with KBG syndrome. Regular ophthalmological examinations are essential to address these concerns promptly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient: Chewing can be challenging for children with KBG syndrome due to weaker jaw muscles and possible tongue-tie. Orthodontic intervention may be considered to correct malocclusion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

a) How this affects the patient: Some children with KBG syndrome exhibit skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger). These conditions contribute to unique anatomical features and functional limitations.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding time is always stressful. She has trouble swallowing sometimes and throws up more often than not.

Parent: Speech is another concern; she started talking later than most children. And overall, she does seem a bit behind her peers in terms of development. I just want to make sure everything is okay and she catches up soon.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews (beginning at age 5).
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
d) Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
e) Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
f) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
g) Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome can develop respiratory infections due to an underdeveloped cilia system, which prevents the airways from clearing bacteria effectively. Frequent upper respiratory tract infections are common, requiring antibiotic treatment for bacterial infections.
- N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- The ANKRD11 gene mutation can lead to various cardiovascular issues, including irregular heartbeat (arrhythmias), enlargement of the heart (cardiomegaly), and weak heart muscle (hypotension).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- A study reported that 15 out of 40 European patients with KBG syndrome had heart-related issues, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities.
- N/A

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- The presence of large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia) can contribute to difficulty cleaning between teeth, increasing the risk of tooth decay and gum disease.
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Immune system dysfunction can increase susceptibility to viral and bacterial infections, leading to frequent illnesses and hospitalizations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Neurological features include brain malformations, seizures, developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural deafness.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- An enlarged third eyelid (meibuddism) can result from chronic inflammation of the tear ducts, causing dry eyes and sensitivity to light.
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Teeth issues, including crowding and difficulty cleaning between teeth, can lead to an increased risk of cavities and periodontal disease.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and challenges with fine motor skills and coordination.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Skeletal features include brachydactyly (short fingers), clinodactyly (curved 5th finger), and an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for thyroid gland issues (due to iodine deficiency).
- Considering orthodontic evaluation for potential bite issues.
- Periodic cardiac evaluations following diagnosis.
- Monitoring for sensorineural deafness and auditory processing disorders.
- Evaluating for cognitive and neurodevelopmental concerns.
- Addressing feeding difficulties and food texture preferences.
- Considering gastrostomy tube placement for nutritional management and ease of administering medications.
- Reviewing cranial ultrasound for possible hydrocephalus.
- Monitoring for hormonal imbalances (e.g., hypothyroidism).
- Conducting periodic vision assessments.
- Evaluating for immunocompetence and vaccine responses.
- Considering physical therapy and occupational therapy interventions.
- Addressing behavioral concerns through therapeutic intervention.
- Reviewing and managing seizures.
- Managing positional plagiocephaly and asymmetrical hip creases.
- Monitoring for palatal concerns and referring for review as indicated.

This completes the clinical report following the specified 13-category schema.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Unfortunately, his teeth seem prone to breaking or chipping easily. We take great care in monitoring his diet and oral hygiene to minimize risks.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There is a valve abnormality in his heart that requires periodic monitoring. Regular check-ups with cardiologists help us stay on top of this condition and adjust treatment as necessary.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

a) Recommendations for Screening and Treatments:

a) How this affects the patient:

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Most children with KBG syndrome do not have a very serious heart condition, but a study of 40 European patients showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions. These included changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers and structural changes.

b) Recommendations:
- Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis. If nothing is found (or already done) this does not need to be repeated.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, which can make meal times challenging. Some children may need shorter periods of playtime to avoid fatigue.

b) Recommendations:
- Consider dietary modifications, such as smaller, more frequent meals, and possible supplementation with vitamins and minerals.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections, and a recent study found that 38% of children with KBG syndrome develop autoimmune diseases. One study suggested that children with KBG syndrome might have a lower threshold for developing autoimmune disease compared to the general population.

b) Recommendations:
- Monitor for autoimmune disorders and consider immunotherapy if autoimmune symptoms develop.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone. It is something we’re working on managing.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia, or low muscle tone, is a common feature in children with KBG syndrome. It can affect a child's ability to perform everyday tasks, such as picking up objects, getting out of bed, and participating in physical activity.

b) Recommendations:
- Consider physiotherapy and occupational therapy to help improve muscle tone and coordination.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more prone to respiratory infections, including pneumonia and sinusitis. They may also experience recurrent otitis media (middle ear infection).

b) Recommendations:
- Monitor for recurrent otitis media and consider antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent episodes.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems are relatively common in people with KBG syndrome. Common issues include astigmatism (irregularly shaped corneas), shortsightedness (myopia), shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and lazy eye (strabismus).

b) Recommendations:
- Regular eye checks and orthoptic assessment (assessment by an ophthalmologist experienced in treating KBG syndrome) should be considered.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

b) Recommendations:
- Regular skin assessments should be carried out, particularly focusing on the scalp, elbows, knees, and creases between the toes.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- His front teeth are larger than usual. That's the main dental issue we're dealing with at the moment.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth size variation is a common feature in people with KBG syndrome. Larger-than-average teeth are quite common, and orthodontic treatment may be necessary.

b) Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluation should be considered.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Education Health Care Plans (EHCP).

b) Recommendations:
- Consider educational needs and potential benefits of specialist provision.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- He has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone. It is something we’re working on managing.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences are common in children with KBG syndrome. Features can include autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction.

b) Recommendations:
- Consider behavioral therapies and strategies to address specific challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Some children with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle). Many children have required short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. It is Unique’s experience that lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- A study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which means that the spinal cord cannot move freely. This can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple and an unusual gait. Most children with KBG syndrome do not have these issues.

b) Recommendations:
- Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine and skull) in children following diagnosis.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
- Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
- Consider a review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
- Consider a review and investigation for neurofibrosis (nerve sheath tumours) given the high incidence of schwannoma (benign tumours arising from Schwann cells) in this condition.
- Consider dietary modification, such as smaller, more frequent meals, and possible vitamin and mineral supplementation.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She has a structural anomaly in her heart, requiring regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She has difficulty chewing hard foods, making it challenging to eat certain textures like apples or meat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Many children with KBG syndrome have difficulty eating tough textures like applesauce or pureed foods.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She experiences seizures, which can be frightening but are manageable with prescribed medications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Approximately 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She faces challenges with chewing solid foods, particularly tougher options like applesauce or pureed foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Many children with KBG syndrome struggle with chewing tough textures like applesauce or pureed foods.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - N/A

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She finds it difficult to chew certain foods, especially harder items like applesauce or pureed foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Many children with KBG syndrome have difficulty eating tough textures like applesauce or pureed foods.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Education Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety are commonly observed in people with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - She exhibits an unusual posture when standing or walking, possibly indicating a spinal issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - A small number of children have experienced an increase in curvature of the spine (scoliosis) and uneven hip creases, suggesting potential spinal issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5.
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.

- Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- One study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which means that the spinal cord cannot move freely. This can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple and an unusual gait. Most children with KBG syndrome do not have these issues.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- KBG syndrome is one of the most prevalent causes of syndromic developmental delay. Most people with KBG syndrome have developmental delay and some element of behavioural differences. ## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- KBG syndrome is caused by changes (variants) in, or a deletion of, the ANKRD11 gene in chromosome 16 (band q24.3). The ANKRD11 gene is responsible for producing a protein called ANKRD11, which plays a role in regulating the immune system. Therefore, people with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune conditions compared to the general population.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: None of the listed symptoms apply to respiratory issues in KBG syndrome.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son experiences fatigue more quickly than other children his age, which could potentially relate to various factors including cardiovascular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of children with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, such as valve changes, chamber holes, or restricted movement of the heart sacs (atrial septal defect).

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has difficulty eating solids, requiring shorter meals and frequent smaller portions. This can lead to nutritional deficiencies and slower weight gain compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, including refusal to eat solid foods, vomiting, regurgitation, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has immunocomplexes, antibodies against kidney proteins, which can trigger autoimmune reactions like nephritis. This requires close monitoring and potential immunotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: One study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome develop immune-related complications, such as nephritis, neuropathy, thyroid dysfunction, and adrenal insufficiency.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son exhibits developmental delays, behavioral differences, and occasional seizures. Neurological evaluations suggest brain connectivity issues affecting cognitive functions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Studies indicate variability in neurodevelopmental outcomes, ranging from mild learning disabilities to profound intellectual disability.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has recurrent otitis media and glue ear, leading to temporary hearing loss and frequent visits to ENT specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome suffer from similar hearing impairments and chronic ear infections.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has astigmatism and shortsightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), contributing to vision challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision abnormalities are relatively common in KBG syndrome patients, with studies reporting prevalence rates ranging from 10% to 75%.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has a distinctive facial appearance characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows that sometimes fuse together.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: The characteristic facial features are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Our son has weak enamel and frequent tooth fractures, necessitating meticulous home care routines and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are prevalent in KBG syndrome patients, with studies reporting high incidences of weak enamel and susceptibility to cavities.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: Our son faces challenges in traditional classroom settings, requiring adaptations such as larger print materials, simplified curriculum content, and additional educational resources.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education levels vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream education and university level qualifications while others require more specialized educational environments.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Our son shows behavioral differences, including autistic-like traits and regression in social skills, which impact interactions and routine behaviors.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the other listed symptoms apply to respiratory issues.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is one of the most prevalent causes of syndromic developmental delay.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is caused by changes (variants) in, or a deletion of, the ANKRD11 gene in chromosome 16 (band q24.3).

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is caused by changes (variants) in, or a deletion of, the ANKRD11 gene in chromosome 16 (band q24.3).

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the other listed symptoms apply to dermatological concerns.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Growing up: Most people with KBG syndrome will enter puberty within the typical age range. For a small number, signs of puberty start at an earlier age than expected ("precocious puberty") and these children should see a pediatrician for review.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education: Children may need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Education Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Behaviour: KBG syndrome can affect behaviour. Children with KBG syndrome may have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behaviour: KBG syndrome can affect behaviour. Children with KBG syndrome may have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Skeletal: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increase in curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal: Growing up: Most people with KBG syndrome will enter puberty within the typical age range. For a small number, signs of puberty start at an earlier age than expected ("precocious puberty") and these children should see a pediatrician for review.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
    - N/A

b) Recommendations for treatments:
    - Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
        - Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
        - Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine and skull) in children following diagnosis.
        - Consider a review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
        - Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
        - Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and behavioural therapy.

Note: The clinical reference guidelines provide comprehensive information on various aspects of KBG syndrome, including medical concerns, management recommendations, and potential implications for other members of the patient's immediate family. Given the unique nature of KBG syndrome, it is crucial for families to consult with geneticists, neurologists, orthodontists, ENT specialists, and other healthcare professionals experienced in managing this condition. Regular follow-up appointments and ongoing assessment are essential to address evolving needs and ensure timely interventions.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience respiratory issues, including recurrent bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and chronic cough. Proper hygiene practices, vaccinations, and timely treatment of respiratory infections are crucial for preventing complications.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient experiences frequent respiratory issues, particularly recurrent bronchiolitis and pneumonia, which can lead to hospitalization and prolonged illness episodes.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to developing respiratory tract infections, especially bronchiolitis, which can result in hospitalization and prolonged illness episodes. Proper hygiene practices, vaccinations, and timely treatment of respiratory infections are essential for managing these conditions.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient shows delayed developmental milestones, specifically concerning fine motor skills such as picking up objects, buttoning clothes, and playing with toys. Additionally, the patient exhibits speech delay, characterized by late onset of babbling, single words, and two-word sentences.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently encounter developmental delays, particularly in the areas of fine motor skills and speech. These challenges underscore the importance of early intervention programs and physical therapy tailored to address these unique needs.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces increased susceptibility to various immunological conditions, including autoimmune diseases and allergies. Given the complexity of the immune system in this population, maintaining a vigilant approach to vaccine administration and avoiding unnecessary stressors is critical.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at heightened risk for developing autoimmune conditions and allergies. Ensuring proper vaccination schedules and minimizing exposure to allergens remains paramount for managing these vulnerabilities.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays a higher incidence of neurological conditions, including seizures, brain anomalies, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Neurological evaluations, including EEG monitoring and imaging, are recommended to identify potential issues early.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to neurological conditions, such as seizures, brain anomalies, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Early identification and management of neurological concerns are vital for optimizing outcomes and ensuring optimal neurological function.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient demonstrates a higher prevalence of ENT-related issues, including recurrent otitis media, nasal congestion, and sinusitis. Addressing these conditions promptly and effectively is crucial for preventing long-term complications and improving overall quality of life.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently encounter respiratory and ear issues, highlighting the importance of thorough evaluation and management of these conditions. Prompt and appropriate interventions can significantly reduce morbidity and improve functional capacity.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits a higher frequency of ocular conditions, including refractive errors, strabismus (eye misalignment), and congenital cataracts. Regular ophthalmic examinations are essential for detecting and treating these conditions promptly.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to develop ocular conditions, emphasizing the significance of comprehensive ophthalmic assessments. Early detection and timely intervention are critical for mitigating visual impairments and enhancing quality of life.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient presents with a higher incidence of skin conditions, including eczema-like patches, keratosis pilaris, and other dermatological manifestations. Routine skincare routines and gentle exfoliation therapies are advised to maintain healthy skin integrity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit dermatological abnormalities, underscoring the necessity for meticulous skincare regimens and gentle exfoliation therapies. Consistent maintenance of skin health is imperative for promoting overall well-being.
    
## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces a higher likelihood of dental issues, including weak enamel, susceptibility to cavities, and irregular tooth development. Dental visits should be scheduled according to age-appropriate intervals to ensure proper oral hygiene and prevent future complications.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more prone to dental problems, necessitating regular dental check-ups and appropriate preventive measures. Maintaining a proactive dental routine is essential for safeguarding oral health and preventing future issues.
    
## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient shows a lower-than-average level of academic achievement, potentially impacting their educational progress and opportunities for formal education. Specialized educational approaches and accommodations are recommended to optimize learning environments and foster personal growth.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently experience educational challenges, affecting their cognitive development and social integration. Tailored educational strategies, including specialized curricula and adaptive teaching methods, are crucial for supporting their unique needs.
    
## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits behavioral traits consistent with the broader KBG syndrome phenotype, including autistic-like behaviors, sensory sensitivities, and temper tantrums. These characteristics contribute to the challenges faced in everyday interactions and play scenarios.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Families dealing with KBG syndrome often observe similar behavioral patterns, adding a layer of understanding and shared experiences among caregivers. Recognizing these traits can facilitate empathy and provide valuable insights into the broader implications of the condition.
    
## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger). These features influence the patient's comfort and ease of movement, contributing to their daily activities and playtime.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome frequently encounter skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis) and short fingers (brachydactyly). These conditions impact the patient's posture and gait, influencing their ability to engage in physically demanding activities and play.
    
## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations:
    - Regular dental check-ups.
    - Regular hearing reviews (beginning at age 5).
    - Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
    - Position of testes examination (consider referral for pediatrician review).
    - Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).

b) Recommendations:
    - Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
    - Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis.
    - Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
    - Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
    - Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with ANKRD11-related syndromes commonly experience gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and delayed gastric emptying. Management strategies should address GERD and delayed gastric emptying.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with ANKRD11-related syndromes are prone to recurrent respiratory tract infections and autoimmune diseases. Immunomodulatory therapies should be considered.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays a reduced tolerance for exercise, indicating potential neurological deficits affecting brain function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with ANKRD11-related syndromes frequently exhibit cognitive delays and behavioral differences. Neurodevelopmental therapy and educational interventions should be prioritized.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with ANKRD11-related syndromes frequently experience refractive errors and ocular motility abnormalities. Regular ophthalmological examinations are crucial.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

a) How this affects the patient: None mentioned.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of patients with KBG syndrome have heart valve abnormalities, holes in the heart chambers, or structural changes requiring monitoring or surgical intervention. [Reference Guidelines].

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly exhibit feeding difficulties and selective eating habits. They may refuse certain textures or tastes, leading to dietary restrictions. Speech delays and sensory integration issues can contribute to swallowing difficulties and the inability to master certain feeding techniques. Dental concerns, including weak enamel and susceptibility to cavities, should be addressed promptly. Regular dental check-ups are crucial for maintaining oral hygiene and preventing infections. [Reference Guidelines].

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions. Management strategies should focus on immunomodulation, vitamin D supplementation, and addressing underlying inflammation. Regular monitoring and early interventions can prevent complications. [Reference Guidelines].

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes in KBG syndrome are characterized by various challenges. Features include cognitive delays, behavioral differences, and sensorimotor dysfunction. Specific treatment options are limited, but multidisciplinary approaches involving physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and educational supports can improve functional abilities and enhance quality of life. [Reference Guidelines].

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can lead to speech delay and difficulty with noisy environments. Audiometric evaluations and hearing aid usage should be considered. Nasal congestion and sinusitis are frequent occurrences and necessitate antibiotic prophylaxis and symptomatic relief. Regular ENT examinations are essential to address potential issues promptly. [Reference Guidelines].

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision-related concerns, such as astigmatism, shortsightedness, and lazy eye (amblyopia), are common. Regular眼科检查和适当的矫正措施对于改善视力至关重要。[参考指南]。

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are prone to skin infections, particularly yeast infections (candidiasis), which can result in white patches on the tongue, lips, and inside the cheeks. Frequent bathing, avoiding sharing towels and personal items, and treating infections promptly are critical. [Reference Guidelines].

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth development and dental health are compromised due to physiological factors. Weak enamel and increased vulnerability to cavities necessitate meticulous oral hygiene practices and regular dental visits. Orthodontic interventions may be necessary to correct craniofacial discrepancies. [Reference Guidelines].

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education experiences vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. While many achieve academic success, those with learning differences require tailored educational plans and accommodations. Transitioning to secondary school presents unique challenges, and consideration of specialized placements or ongoing support is warranted. [Reference Guidelines].

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural and developmental characteristics can manifest differently across individuals. Common traits include autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-like behaviors, sensory processing issues, and executive function deficits. Early identification and targeted therapies can mitigate some symptoms. [Reference Guidelines].

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), can impact posture and gait. Monitoring for kyphosis (hunchback) and ensuring proper footwear are important considerations. [Reference Guidelines].

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening: Regular dental check-ups, audiometry, and periodic cardiovascular assessments.
b) Treatments: Addressing sensory integration issues, managing behavior and developmental challenges, providing appropriate educational support, considering orthodontic interventions, and managing vision and hearing concerns.
